note: Crash report v3 (#13379) is a native app's report: the iPhone and Mac apps' crashes as MetricKit hands them over on a later launch. The app posts a dump (below) to POST /api/playtest/app-crash, and the API makes the report from it with the codec and keeps it by bucket like every other report. Its frames carry no names: a frame is the binary and the frame's offset in it, `f BINARY +0xOFFSET`, and the `build` line is the UUID of the app's own binary, which names the dSYM that resolves its frames (coax/web/symbols.sh app-frame). The signature is the kind and the three innermost frames in the app's own binary, each BINARY+0xOFFSET (the three innermost of any binary when none is the app's). Offsets change with every build, so one bug in two builds lands in two buckets. A room's report stays v1 and a page's v2; `source app` is only ever v3. The Android app (#13379) sends the same dump from the tombstone the system keeps of a native crash (ApplicationExitInfo, apps/shared/host/android/crash-reports.c and crash-dump.coax): `app android`, the signal in Linux's numbering, and each frame's binary named by its GNU build ID in place of a UUID. Its `build` line is the build ID of the app's own library, which names the unstripped library kept for it (coax/web/symbols.sh android, android-frame). That widened `app` and `build` without a new version: every report made before it is still a v3 report, and the one codec on the server makes every report.

ios, mac or android
the system's version as MetricKit names it; on Android "Android RELEASE (API LEVEL)"
the app's version
the app's build number
the name of the app's own binary
the signal's number, in the system's own numbering (Apple's; Linux's on Android)
the Mach exception's type
the termination reason

UUID OFFSET BINARY: a frame of the crashed thread, innermost first; the binary's UUID (dashes and either case allowed), the offset into the binary in decimal, the binary's name; on Android the first word is the binary's GNU build ID in hex (8 to 64 digits), or 0 when it has none
when it crashed, Unix ms
app
ios, mac or android
the system's version
VERSION (BUILD), the app's version and build number; ? when unknown
the UUID of the app's own binary, 32 lowercase hex digits; on Android the GNU build ID of the app's own library, 8 to 64 lowercase hex digits; 0 when no frame is in it
the signal's name (SIGSEGV, SIGABRT...), EXC for a Mach exception with no signal, else crash
the termination reason
BINARY +0xOFFSET (the offset into the binary, lowercase hex); innermost first, at most 24
KIND|BINARY+0xOFFSET, up to three: the innermost frames in the app's own binary, or of any binary when none is; KIND|TEXT when there is no frame
